newsitem.title: CANADA: Great Lakes restructures Mexican assets.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes restructures Mexican assets.

text.p: Great Lakes Minerals Inc said on Thursday it plans to reorganize the company to help raise more equity to develop and explore its gold and silver properties in Mexico.
The move will also help with the repayment of the company's debts, Great Lakes said in a statement.
Shareholders are to vote on the changes on January 29.

Great Lakes said it plans to sell its Mexican assets to Newmex Mining Co, a newly formed wholly owned subsidiary of Great Lakes, in a transaction worth C$16.35 million. Newmex will hold 100 percent of both the Lluvia de oro and the Palmarito projects.
Payment will be through a C$14.5 million note and one million Newmex shares worth C$2 per share.
Great Lakes said it will distribute the one million Newmex shares to its shareholders as a stock dividend.
The reorganization will also give Great Lakes Minerals shareholders right to acquire 8,250,000 shares for C$2 each.
Newmex will pay C$14 million and issue 175,000 shares for C$2 each to raise the C$14.35 million it needs to give Great Lakes.
Great Lakes said it will distribute its 175,000 Newmex shares to the holders of its C$10 million 7 percent convertible debentures to fully pay interest owed.
Great Lakes said it will use C$14 million received from Newmex to repay the C$10 million principal amount of the debentures and satisfy other liabilities.
A balance of C$500,000 will be used for working capital.
